Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi on Tuesday, July 28, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue an orange alert for the national capital for the next few hours.
Dark clouds covered the city through the morning as moderate to heavy showers continued. According to the IMD, Delhi weather today is expected to remain cloudy, with moderate rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds over the next few hours.
Delhi rains today: Waterlogging slows traffic in several areas
Heavy rainfall also led to waterlogging in parts of the national capital, affecting traffic movement during the morning rush.
Visuals shared by ANI showed vehicles moving through waterlogged stretches near Vayu Bhawan, with commuters navigating rain-soaked roads amid persistent showers. Water accumulation at several locations affected the flow of traffic.
PTI also shared visuals of rain lashing parts of the city near AIIMS, while another video showed waterlogging on Tolstoy Marg following the heavy downpour.
According to IMD data, Safdarjung, the city's primary weather station, recorded 32.4 mm of cumulative rainfall till 8:30 am on Tuesday.
Other rainfall figures included:
Ridge: 37.6 mm
Lodi Road: 36.7 mm
Ayanagar: 4.0 mm
Palam: 0.8 mm
On Monday, between 8:30 am and 5:30 pm, Ridge received 19.4 mm of rainfall, followed by Lodi Road (11.5 mm), Safdarjung (8.0 mm) and Ayanagar (3.8 mm), while Palam recorded no rainfall during that period.
The rainfall is part of the ongoing Delhi monsoon activity that has brought frequent showers to the city in recent days.
Delhi weather: Minimum temperature stays below normal
The minimum temperature at Safdarjung settled at 25.5 degrees Celsius, which was 1.8 degrees below normal, according to IMD data.
The continuing rain has also kept weather conditions relatively pleasant compared with recent weeks.
Delhi weather today: AQI remains in satisfactory category
The rainfall also helped keep air quality at a better level.
According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 77 at 9 am, placing it in the 'satisfactory' category.
An AQI between 51 and 100 is considered satisfactory.
Delhi rain alert: Geeta Colony building tilts after heavy showers
Heavy rain also triggered a building safety scare in east Delhi.
A four-storey building in Geeta Colony tilted on Monday evening, prompting a rescue operation in which all occupants were safely evacuated, police said on Tuesday.
The incident took place in Akhade Wali Gali, where authorities cordoned off the area and advised residents of neighbouring buildings to stay away from the structure.
Police said an elderly woman with a spinal injury was among those rescued safely.
Residents say part of building collapsed before it began leaning
According to residents quoted by PTI, an overhang (chhajja) above a second-floor balcony collapsed due to the rain, after which the building started leaning.
Residents also claimed they had earlier complained to authorities about the condition of the building, which they said was around 30 to 35 years old.
Visuals from the spot showed the corner building, with shops on the ground floor and residential floors above, leaning towards one side while police personnel kept people away from the area.
Delhi weather forecast: More rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds likely
According to the IMD, Delhi weather is expected to remain overcast over the next few hours, with moderate rainfall, thunderstorms and gusty winds.
With more rain forecast, authorities are monitoring the situation, while residents have been advised to stay alert, avoid waterlogged areas where possible and follow official weather advisories.

title: Delhi Weather Today: Rain To Lash Capital-NCR As IMD Issues Yellow Alert; Waterlogging, Traffic Disruptions Li - Times Now
full_text:
People across Delhi-NCR woke up to cloudy skies and scattered showers on Tuesday, July 28, as a fresh spell of monsoon rain brought much-needed relief from the lingering humidity. Following intermittent rainfall earlier this month, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert, forecasting more rain over the next few hours. Meteorologists said the morning rain band had largely shifted towards east Delhi and east NCR, leaving behind showers in isolated parts of the capital. However, with favourable monsoon conditions continuing, more showers are expected through the day.
A woman carries a child during rainfall near India Gate, in New Delhi
This comes a day after rain lashed several parts of the national capital on Monday afternoon, bringing much-needed relief from the scorching heat after temperatures had climbed well above normal earlier in the day.
What alerts has the IMD issued for Delhi-NCR?
How has the recent rain affected traffic in Delhi?
What is the expected weather pattern for the week?
Moderate Rain Forecast, Temperatures To Dip
According to the IMD's latest forecast, Delhi is expected to record a maximum temperature between 32 and 34 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to remain between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius.The weather department has predicted one or two spells of very light to light rain across most parts of the city, with moderate rainfall likely at a few places during the early morning to noon hours. Another spell of light to moderate rain is expected towards the evening and night, particularly at isolated locations.
Surface winds are expected to blow at 15-20 kmph, providing some relief from the humid conditions.
Monday's Rain Brings Relief After Hot Weather
Delhi experienced a hot and humid start to Monday before rain swept across many areas in the afternoon.According to the IMD, the Ridge weather station recorded the highest rainfall at 19.4 mm till 5.30 pm, followed by Lodhi Road with 11.5 mm and Safdarjung with 8 mm. Other areas, including Pusa (4 mm), Ayanagar (3.8 mm), Janakpuri (2 mm) and parts of Mayur Vihar, Narayana and Najafgarh, also received light showers. However, localities such as Palam, Jafarpur and Chhatarpur remained dry during the same period.
Before the rain arrived, Safdarjung recorded a maximum temperature of 38.1 degrees Celsius, which was 3.2 degrees above the seasonal average. Palam and Lodhi Road both touched 37.2 degrees Celsius, while the Ridge and Ayanagar recorded 36.4 degrees Celsius. The minimum temperature at Safdarjung settled at 28.6 degrees Celsius, 1.3 degrees above normal.
Waterlogging, Traffic Delays Expected
The IMD has warned of minor traffic disruptions due to rain and possible water accumulation on roads and in low-lying areas. Motorists have been advised to check traffic conditions before leaving, follow official advisories and avoid routes that are prone to waterlogging.Meanwhile, Delhi's air quality worsened slightly, with the 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) standing at 101, placing it in the 'moderate' category for the second consecutive day, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
The rainy spell is expected to continue over the next few days, with moderate rainfall likely on Wednesday, followed by light to moderate showers through the remainder of the week, helping keep daytime temperatures largely in the 32-35 degrees Celsius range.
